title: Psalms Chapter 74 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 74 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 74 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 74.

questions.question: Who is the author or attributed writer of Psalms 74 according to the chapter heading?
questions.correctAnswer: Asaph
questions.explanation: The chapter heading notes this Psalm as a Maschil of Asaph, indicating he is the author (Psalms 74:1).

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God about His anger in Psalms 74?
options: Why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
Why hast Thou forgotten to be merciful?
Why dost Thou punish the wicked?
questions.correctAnswer: Why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
questions.explanation: The psalmist specifically asks why God's anger smokes against the sheep of His pasture (Psalms 74:1).

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to remember in Psalms 74:2?
options: Thy congregation which thou hast purchased of old
questions.correctAnswer: Thy congregation which thou hast purchased of old
questions.explanation: The psalmist requests God to remember His congregation, which He purchased of old (Psalms 74:2).

questions.question: According to Psalms 74:3, what has the enemy done in the sanctuary?
questions.correctAnswer: Wickedly done perpetual desolations
questions.explanation: The verse describes the enemy's wicked actions causing perpetual desolations in the sanctuary (Psalms 74:3).

questions.question: In Psalms 74:4, what do the enemies do in the midst of God's congregations?
options: Roar and set up their ensigns for signs
questions.correctAnswer: Roar and set up their ensigns for signs
questions.explanation: The enemies roar in the midst of God's congregations and set up their ensigns as signs (Psalms 74:4).

questions.question: What made a man famous according to Psalms 74:5?
options: Lifting up axes upon the thick trees
questions.correctAnswer: Lifting up axes upon the thick trees
questions.explanation: A man was famous as he had lifted up axes upon the thick trees (Psalms 74:5).

questions.question: What instruments are used to break down the carved work in Psalms 74:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Axes and hammers
questions.explanation: The carved work was broken down at once with axes and hammers (Psalms 74:6).

questions.question: What did the enemies do to the sanctuary as described in Psalms 74:7?
options: Cast fire into it and defiled it
questions.correctAnswer: Cast fire into it and defiled it
questions.explanation: The enemies cast fire into the sanctuary and defiled it by casting down the dwelling place of God's name (Psalms 74:7).

questions.question: What did the enemies say in their hearts according to Psalms 74:8?
options: Let us build a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: Let us destroy them together
questions.explanation: They said in their hearts, 'Let us destroy them together' and burned all synagogues of God (Psalms 74:8).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 74:9 states that there are still many prophets among the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:9 says there is no more any prophet among them.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist asks God how long the enemy shall blaspheme His name in Psalms 74:10.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The psalmist questions how long the enemy will blaspheme God's name (Psalms 74:10).

questions.question: Which of these actions is mentioned first in Psalms 74 as done by God?
options: Preparing the light and the sun
Setting all the borders of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Dividing the sea by strength
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:13 states first that God divided the sea by His strength.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 74:17 states that God has made summer and winter.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:17 says God has set all the borders of the earth and made summer and winter.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God not to forget in Psalms 74:19?
questions.correctAnswer: The congregation of the poor
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:19 asks God not to forget the congregation of the poor forever.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 74:22 commands God to arise and plead His own cause.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The psalmist calls for God to arise and plead His own cause (Psalms 74:22).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 74 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 74 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 74:9, what is notably absent among the people?
options: Any prophets and those who know how long
questions.correctAnswer: Any prophets and those who know how long
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:9 states, 'We see not our signs: there is no more any prophet: neither is there among us any that knoweth how long,' indicating the absence of prophets and those who understand the duration of their suffering.

questions.question: What is the main plea in Psalms 74:10 regarding the adversary's actions?
options: That God ends the blasphemy and reproach
That the people ignore the adversary
That the adversary continue to reproach
questions.correctAnswer: That God ends the blasphemy and reproach
questions.explanation: Verse 10 asks, 'O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?' showing a plea for God to stop the adversary's blasphemy and reproach.

questions.question: In Psalms 74:11, what metaphor is used to describe God's action that the psalmist desires Him to take?
options: Withdraw thy hand, even thy right hand
Lift up thy sword and fight
Pour out your spirit upon us
questions.correctAnswer: Withdraw thy hand, even thy right hand
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'Why withdrawest thou thy hand, even thy right hand? pluck it out of thy bosom,' which is a metaphorical plea for God to act decisively instead of withdrawing.

questions.question: How does Psalms 74:12 describe God’s role in the world?
options: God is King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth
God is a distant judge who does not intervene
God is a silent observer of human affairs
God is only concerned with the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: God is King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth
questions.explanation: Verse 12 affirms God's sovereignty and active role: 'For God is my King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth,' highlighting faith and trust in God's continual salvation.

questions.question: What mighty act is attributed to God in Psalms 74:13?
options: Dividing the sea by strength and breaking the heads of dragons in the waters
Creating the heavens and the earth
Parting the Red Sea for the Israelites
Sending fire to consume the enemy
questions.correctAnswer: Dividing the sea by strength and breaking the heads of dragons in the waters
questions.explanation: Verse 13 describes God's power: 'Thou didst divide the sea by thy strength: thou brakest the heads of the dragons in the waters,' demonstrating His control over chaos and evil.

questions.question: What does Psalms 74:14 say God did to Leviathan?
options: Broke his heads in pieces and gave him as meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness
Let him roam freely in the sea
Made him king of the waters
questions.correctAnswer: Broke his heads in pieces and gave him as meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states, 'Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces, and gavest him to be meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness,' symbolizing God's victory over chaos and provision for His people.

questions.question: What natural phenomena does Psalms 74:15 attribute to God's power?
options: He cleaved the fountain and the flood and dried up mighty rivers
He created the mountains and valleys
He caused the sun to stand still
He formed the clouds and rain
questions.correctAnswer: He cleaved the fountain and the flood and dried up mighty rivers
questions.explanation: Verse 15 acknowledges God's control over waters: 'Thou didst cleave the fountain and the flood: thou driedst up mighty rivers,' emphasizing His sovereign power in nature.

questions.question: According to Psalms 74:16, what has God prepared?
questions.correctAnswer: The light and the sun
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'The day is thine, the night also is thine: thou hast prepared the light and the sun,' showing God's creative authority over day and night.

questions.question: How does Psalms 74:17 describe God's role in the seasons and boundaries of the earth?
options: He set all the borders of the earth and made summer and winter
He created only the spring and fall
He left the earth's seasons to chance
questions.correctAnswer: He set all the borders of the earth and made summer and winter
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states, 'Thou hast set all the borders of the earth: thou hast made summer and winter,' affirming God's sovereign control over creation's order.

questions.question: In light of Psalms 74:9-10, what spiritual lesson about patience and faith can a believer learn?
options: To trust God even when signs and prophets seem absent and enemies blaspheme
To abandon faith when no signs are seen
To rely solely on human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: To trust God even when signs and prophets seem absent and enemies blaspheme
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 show a lament over absent prophets and ongoing enemy blasphemy, encouraging believers to maintain faith and patience despite apparent silence and opposition.

questions.question: What does the plea in Psalms 74:11 teach about prayer and dependence on God during adversity?
options: To ask God to stop withdrawing and act powerfully on our behalf
To stop praying if God seems distant
To only pray when circumstances are good
questions.correctAnswer: To ask God to stop withdrawing and act powerfully on our behalf
questions.explanation: Verse 11 pleads, 'Why withdrawest thou thy hand...,' teaching believers to earnestly seek God's intervention and not lose hope when He seems distant.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 74:12-13, how can recalling God's past mighty deeds help a believer facing trials?
options: It strengthens faith by remembering God’s power to save and control chaos
It shows that God no longer acts
It suggests trials are permanent and unchangeable
questions.correctAnswer: It strengthens faith by remembering God’s power to save and control chaos
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 recall God's saving acts and power over the sea and dragons, encouraging believers to trust God's ability to overcome present difficulties.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 74:14 portrays God as victorious over Leviathan, symbolizing triumph over evil forces.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes God breaking Leviathan’s heads and giving it as food, symbolizing His victory over evil and provision for His people.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 74:15, God is powerless over natural waters and floods.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 15 clearly attributes control over waters to God, stating He cleaved fountains and dried mighty rivers, showing His power over nature.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 74:16-17 affirm God’s sovereignty over time, seasons, and the boundaries of the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: These verses affirm God’s control over day and night, light and sun, and the setting of earth’s borders and seasons, highlighting His sovereignty.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 74 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 74.

questions.question: According to Psalms 74:17, what has God set upon the earth?
options: All the borders of the earth and made summer and winter
The foundations of the mountains and rivers
questions.correctAnswer: All the borders of the earth and made summer and winter
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:17 clearly states that God has set all the borders of the earth and made summer and winter, emphasizing His sovereign control over the natural order.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to remember in Psalms 74:18?
options: That the enemy has reproached and foolish people have blasphemed His name
questions.correctAnswer: That the enemy has reproached and foolish people have blasphemed His name
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:18 specifically requests God to remember that the enemy reproaches Him and foolish people blaspheme His name, highlighting the psalmist’s plea for divine intervention.

questions.question: In Psalms 74:19, what is the 'turtledove' a metaphor for?
options: The congregation or people of God
questions.correctAnswer: The congregation or people of God
questions.explanation: The 'turtledove' in Psalms 74:19 metaphorically represents the congregation or the people of God, whom the psalmist asks God not to deliver to the wicked.

questions.question: What does the psalmist request God to have respect to in Psalms 74:20?
questions.correctAnswer: The covenant
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:20 explicitly asks God to have respect unto the covenant, linking God’s promises to His people with their present suffering.

questions.question: According to Psalms 74:21, what should not happen to the oppressed?
questions.correctAnswer: They should not return ashamed
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:21 petitions that the oppressed not return ashamed, emphasizing God's justice and care for the needy.

questions.question: In Psalms 74:22, what is God asked to do regarding His own cause?
options: Arise and plead His own cause
questions.correctAnswer: Arise and plead His own cause
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:22 calls on God to arise and plead His own cause, reminding Him of how He is reproached daily by the foolish.

questions.question: What is increasing continually according to Psalms 74:23?
options: The tumult of those that rise up against God
questions.correctAnswer: The tumult of those that rise up against God
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:23 states that the tumult of enemies rises continually, showing the increasing opposition against God and His people.

questions.question: The description in Psalms 74:13-14 of God breaking the heads of dragons and leviathan is an example of which literary device?
options: Typology illustrating God's power over chaos
Simile comparing God to a warrior
Metaphor for the destruction of enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Typology illustrating God's power over chaos
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:13-14 uses the imagery of God breaking the heads of dragons and leviathan as a typological reference to His sovereign power over chaotic forces, a common theme in ancient Near Eastern literature.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God controlling the seasons as seen in Psalms 74:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 8:22
questions.explanation: Genesis 8:22 talks about the natural order continuing with seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, which echoes the theme of God's control over the seasons as in Psalms 74:17.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'turtledove' in Psalms 74:19 symbolize in the Old Testament?
options: Innocence and the congregation of God's people
questions.correctAnswer: Innocence and the congregation of God's people
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'turtledove' often symbolizes innocence and purity, and in Psalms 74:19 it represents God's vulnerable congregation needing protection.

questions.question: How does Psalms 74:20 describe the 'dark places of the earth'?
options: As full of the habitations of cruelty
As places of refuge for the righteous
As lands of peace and plenty
questions.correctAnswer: As full of the habitations of cruelty
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:20 describes the dark places of the earth as full of cruelty, highlighting the danger and oppression present in the world.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 74:21 calls for the poor and needy to be ashamed of their plight.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:21 actually prays that the oppressed not return ashamed, but rather that the poor and needy praise God's name, opposing the idea of shame.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 74:12 declares God as King from old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:12 proclaims God as King of old who works salvation on earth, affirming His eternal reign and saving power.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with the theme of God defending His cause against reproach as in Psalms 74:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 3:4
questions.explanation: Romans 3:4 echoes the theme of God's righteousness and defense of His name against reproach, aligning with Psalms 74:22's call for God to plead His own cause.

questions.question: What historical context does Psalms 74 likely reflect based on the destruction described in verses 6-8?
options: The destruction of the temple by the Babylonians
questions.correctAnswer: The destruction of the temple by the Babylonians
questions.explanation: The references to the sanctuary being defiled and synagogues burned in Psalms 74:6-8 reflect the historical context of the Babylonian destruction of the temple.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 74 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 74 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is emphasized in Psalms 74:12 where God is called 'my King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:12 calls God 'my King of old' which emphasizes His sovereign rule over all creation and history, as He actively works salvation in the earth.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by the imagery of God 'dividing the sea' and 'breaking the heads of leviathan' in Psalms 74:13-14?
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of creation's subjugation
questions.explanation: Verses 74:13-14 depict God’s power over chaotic forces symbolized by sea monsters, teaching that God has sovereign control over creation and chaos, subduing all powers.

questions.question: How does Psalms 74:16-17 contribute to our understanding of God's providence?
options: God actively orders time and nature
God is limited to spiritual matters only
questions.correctAnswer: God actively orders time and nature
questions.explanation: Verses 74:16-17 state God has prepared day and night and set the borders of the earth, showing His providential control over natural order and seasons.

questions.question: In Psalms 74:1, the psalmist asks why God has 'cast us off forever' and why His anger 'smokes against the sheep of His pasture.' What theological reality is this lament highlighting?
options: The experience of divine judgment and abandonment
questions.correctAnswer: The experience of divine judgment and abandonment
questions.explanation: Psalms 74:1 expresses the community’s sense of being forsaken by God and subjected to His wrath, highlighting the reality of divine judgment upon His people.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth about God's covenant care does Psalms 74:2 and Psalms 74:19 teach?
options: God forgets His people when they suffer
God protects His purchased inheritance and cares for the poor
God’s covenant is ineffective in hardship
God’s people are independent of divine help
questions.correctAnswer: God protects His purchased inheritance and cares for the poor
questions.explanation: Verse 74:2 speaks of God's purchased congregation and heritage, while 74:19 pleads for God to not forget His poor congregation, together teaching God's covenant care for His redeemed people including the vulnerable.

questions.question: What do Psalms 74:4-8 reveal about the nature of spiritual warfare against God's sanctuary?
options: Enemies openly attack and defile the sanctuary with violence and fire
Enemies are indifferent to the sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: Enemies openly attack and defile the sanctuary with violence and fire
questions.explanation: Verses 74:4-8 describe enemies roaring amidst God's people, breaking down carved work, casting fire into the sanctuary, and burning synagogues, showing violent opposition to God's dwelling.

questions.question: According to Psalms 74:9, what spiritual crisis does the people experience regarding prophetic guidance?
options: Prophets abound and guide the people
No prophets remain and the people lack knowledge of God's plan
Prophetic messages are clear and certain
questions.correctAnswer: No prophets remain and the people lack knowledge of God's plan
questions.explanation: Verse 74:9 states there are no more prophets and no one knows how long the affliction will last, indicating a crisis of prophetic guidance and spiritual uncertainty.

questions.question: What does the plea in Psalms 74:20 for God to 'have respect unto the covenant' teach about the importance of divine promises amid human suffering?
options: Divine covenants are irrelevant during suffering
Divine covenants provide hope and assurance in dark times
questions.correctAnswer: Divine covenants provide hope and assurance in dark times
questions.explanation: Verse 74:20 appeals to God's covenant as a basis for hope despite the 'dark places' full of cruelty, teaching that covenant promises sustain faith amid suffering.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by synthesizing Psalms 74:10 and 74:22 regarding the problem of the enemy's reproach against God?
options: God is called to actively defend His honor against persistent blasphemy
The enemy's reproach strengthens God's kingdom
Believers should respond with silence only
questions.correctAnswer: God is called to actively defend His honor against persistent blasphemy
questions.explanation: Verses 74:10 and 74:22 both lament and call God to arise and plead His cause against daily reproach, emphasizing the need for God’s active defense of His holy name.

questions.question: What does Psalms 74:15 teach about God's power over natural elements?
options: God cleaves fountains and dries mighty rivers
God only controls the sun and moon
God creates but does not sustain nature
questions.correctAnswer: God cleaves fountains and dries mighty rivers
questions.explanation: Verse 74:15 describes God’s power to cleave fountains and flood and dry up mighty rivers, demonstrating divine sovereignty over natural forces.

questions.question: Which doctrine of God is underscored in Psalms 74:18-19 where God is reminded that enemies have reproached and blasphemed His name, and the congregation is petitioned not to be forgotten?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 74:18-19 remind God of the reproach and blasphemy by enemies and plead for remembrance of His people, highlighting His just character and covenant commitment.

questions.question: How does Psalms 74:21 relate to the doctrine of sanctification and God's purposes for His people?
options: God ignores the poor and needy
God desires that the poor and needy praise His name, reflecting sanctification
God's people should not praise Him in suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God desires that the poor and needy praise His name, reflecting sanctification
questions.explanation: Verse 74:21 petitions God so the oppressed and needy will not return ashamed but praise His name, indicating sanctification includes worship and a transformed life despite hardship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 74 portrays a God who is absent in times of crisis. What does Psalms 74:11-12 actually teach about God's presence and power in adversity?
options: God has withdrawn and is powerless
God is King of old, working salvation, though His hand seems withdrawn
God is unaware of human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God is King of old, working salvation, though His hand seems withdrawn
questions.explanation: Verses 74:11-12 describe the psalmist's cry about God's hand withdrawing, but affirm God as eternal King actively working salvation, showing divine presence despite apparent silence.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine judgment and deliverance emerges from Psalms 74:7-8 and Psalms 74:22-23?
options: God allows enemies to destroy but will arise to plead and remember His cause
questions.correctAnswer: God allows enemies to destroy but will arise to plead and remember His cause
questions.explanation: Verses 74:7-8 describe the sanctuary's destruction by enemies, while 74:22-23 call God to arise and remember the reproach, teaching that divine judgment and eventual deliverance are part of God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: What does Psalms 74:6 teach about the nature of the enemy's assault on God's sanctuary?
options: Enemies break down the carved work with axes and hammers swiftly
Enemies pray for the sanctuary's protection
questions.correctAnswer: Enemies break down the carved work with axes and hammers swiftly
questions.explanation: Verse 74:6 states enemies break down the sanctuary's carved work suddenly and violently, showing the destructive and aggressive nature of their attack.
